newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: BASF plans new plants in Philippines, Korea.
newsitem.headline: BASF plans new plants in Philippines, Korea.

text.p: German chemicals group BASF AG said on Friday it planned two new acrylate dispersion plants, each with annual capacity of 25,000 tonnes, in the Philippines and South Korea at a cost of 20 million marks apiece.
The company had also recently signed letters of intent for the construction of new plants in China and Malaysia that will produce acrylic acids, said BASF Philippine managing director Jaime Mendoza.
BASF said the plants would further strengthen the company's position in Southeast Asia. It already has production plants in China, Indonesia, Australia, India, Japan, and Pakistan.
The Philippine acyrlate dispersions plant, located in Canlubang, Laguna province south of Manila, was expected to start commercial operations in the first quarter of 1999, Mendoza said.
Mendoza told Reuters the plant in South Korea was expected to be onstream almost at the same time as the Philippine plant.
Acrylate dispersions are used in the paint and adhesives industries.
Mendoza said the plants would source raw materials, mainly acrylic acid and acrylic esters, from BASF's Asian plants.
